questions.statement: Choose the sentence that correctly uses the present perfect for experience.
questions.context: Practica de presente perfecto, Quito, grado 11.

options.text: Did you ever eat a cuy in Ecuador?
options.feedback: 'Did' plus base verb refers to a finished past event.

options.text: Are you ever eating a cuy in Ecuador?
options.feedback: The present continuous is not used for life experience.

options.text: Have you ever eaten a cuy in Ecuador?
options.feedback: Auxiliary 'have' plus participle 'eaten' is the structure for life experience.

options.text: Do you ever eat a cuy in Ecuador?
options.feedback: That form speaks about a habit, not about past experience.

questions.explanation:
'Have you ever...' expresa una experiencia de vida sin tiempo definido, que corresponde al presente perfecto.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'She ____ (never / be) to the Galapagos Islands.'

options.text: has never been
options.feedback: 'Has never been' is the correct structure for a life experience with 'never'.

options.text: has never be
options.feedback: The second verb must be the past participle 'been'.

options.text: is never being
options.feedback: The present continuous cannot express a life experience.

options.text: was never
options.feedback: The simple past would imply a specific past time.

questions.explanation:
La experiencia de vida con 'never' se forma con 'has never been', donde 'been' es el participio de 'be'.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What is the difference between 'I have been to Paris' and 'I have gone to Paris'?

options.text: Both mean the person is currently in Paris
options.feedback: Only 'have gone' places the person in Paris at the time of speaking.

options.text: 'Have been' refers to the future and 'have gone' to the past
options.feedback: Both forms refer to past actions connected with the present.

options.text: 'Have gone' is the simple past of 'go'
options.feedback: 'Have gone' is a present perfect form, not a simple past.

options.text: 'Have been' is experience; 'have gone' means the person is there now
options.feedback: The difference lies in whether the person returned.

questions.explanation:
'Have been' indica experiencia sin decir si se sigue alli; 'have gone' indica que la persona esta alli ahora.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct question with the present perfect.

options.text: Did you finish the project yet?
options.feedback: 'Did' requires the base form 'finish' and a past time.

options.text: Have you finished the project yet?
options.feedback: Auxiliary before the subject and participle 'finished' with 'yet'.

options.text: Are you finish the project yet?
options.feedback: 'Are' cannot be combined with the participle 'finished'.

options.text: Do you finished the project yet?
options.feedback: 'Do' plus participle is not a valid structure.

questions.explanation:
La pregunta conserva el auxiliar 'have' delante del sujeto y el participio despues. Es uno de los puntos mas frecuentes de las pruebas de esta unidad.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Look at the sentence: 'I have seen that film three times.' What does 'three times' tell us?
questions.context: Cantidad y frecuencia en presente perfecto, Guayaquil.

options.text: How many times the action has occurred
options.feedback: Counting experiences is a standard use of the present perfect.

options.text: How long the action lasted
options.feedback: Duration would be expressed with 'for' plus a period.

options.text: When the action will happen
options.feedback: The present perfect does not refer to the future.

options.text: That the action is happening now
options.feedback: The counting refers to repeated past occurrences.

questions.explanation:
'Three times' cuantifica cuantas veces se ha producido la accion, una funcion tipica del presente perfecto.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which time expression is NOT normally used with the present perfect?

options.text: ever
options.feedback: 'Ever' is a present perfect marker used in questions about experience.

options.text: yesterday
options.feedback: A finished past moment requires the simple past, not the present perfect.

options.text: just
options.feedback: 'Just' is a present perfect marker meaning very recently.

options.text: already
options.feedback: 'Already' is a present perfect marker meaning sooner than expected.

questions.explanation:
'Yesterday' fija un momento del pasado, por lo que es incompatible con el presente perfecto.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the dialogue: 'A: Have you ever been to the Galapagos? B: Yes, I ____ there in 2019.'

options.text: went
options.feedback: 'Went' is the simple past required by the closed past time 'in 2019'.

options.text: have gone
options.feedback: The present perfect is incompatible with a finished past year.

options.text: am going
options.feedback: The present continuous places the action now, but the text says 2019.

options.text: had gone
options.feedback: The past perfect would need another past reference point, which is absent.

questions.explanation:
Como 'in 2019' es un tiempo pasado definido, la segunda oracion va en pasado simple: 'went'.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence is correct with 'since'?

options.text: I live in Quito since I was born.
options.feedback: The simple present is not compatible with 'since' plus a past reference.

options.text: I am living in Quito since I was born.
options.feedback: The present continuous cannot be combined with 'since' in this usage.

options.text: I live in Quito since my birth.
options.feedback: 'Since' does not take 'my birth' in that construction.

options.text: I have lived in Quito since I was born.
options.feedback: 'Have lived since' states a situation that began in the past and continues.

questions.explanation:
'Since' introduce un punto de partida en el tiempo y por eso se combina con presente perfecto o pasado simple.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which option is the correct present perfect form?

options.text: We have know each other since primary school.
options.feedback: After 'have' the participle 'known' is required.

options.text: We are know each other since primary school.
options.feedback: 'Are' plus participle is not a valid verb group.

options.text: We have known each other from last year ago
options.feedback: 'Since' does not combine with 'ago' in the same expression.

options.text: We have known each other since primary school.
options.feedback: 'Have known' plus 'since' expresses a situation continuing from the past.

questions.explanation:
Solo la opcion que combina 'have' con un participio es una estructura de presente perfecto valida.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What does the word 'yet' express in 'She has not arrived yet'?

options.text: The action will never happen
options.feedback: 'Yet' does not exclude a future occurrence.

options.text: The action happened in the past
options.feedback: 'Not ... yet' negates a completed past occurrence.

options.text: The action has not happened up to now
options.feedback: 'Yet' places the non-occurrence at the present moment.

options.text: The action happens every day
options.feedback: 'Yet' has no relation to daily frequency.

questions.explanation:
'Yet' indica que la accion esperada no se ha producido hasta el momento actual. Esta estructura se repite con otros verbos del mismo grupo.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct form: 'They ____ in this city for ten years.'

options.text: lived
options.feedback: The simple past would not indicate that the situation still continues.

options.text: have lived
options.feedback: 'Have lived' plus 'for' expresses a situation that began in the past and continues.

options.text: are living
options.feedback: The present continuous is possible but 'for ten years' fits the present perfect better.

options.text: had lived
options.feedback: The past perfect would place the situation before another past reference.

questions.explanation:
La duracion con 'for' y la continuacion de la situacion en el presente exigen presente perfecto.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence correctly uses 'just'?
questions.context: Uso de 'just' en presente perfecto, Guayaquil.

options.text: The results have just arrived.
options.feedback: 'Have just arrived' marks a very recent completed action.

options.text: The results have arrived just.
options.feedback: The adverb must sit between the auxiliary and the participle.

options.text: The results just have arrived.
options.feedback: The correct order is auxiliary plus adverb plus participle.

options.text: The results have just arrive.
options.feedback: The verb must be the participle 'arrived'.

questions.explanation:
'Just' se coloca entre el auxiliar y el participio y expresa una accion muy reciente.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What is the function of the present perfect in the sentence: 'I have lost my keys, so I cannot enter'?
questions.context: Analisis de la funcion del tiempo, Quito.

options.text: It describes a daily routine
options.feedback: A routine belongs to the simple present.

options.text: It places the action in the distant past
options.feedback: A distant past event would use the simple past with a date.

options.text: It expresses a future plan
options.feedback: No future element appears in the sentence.

options.text: It links a past action to its present result
options.feedback: That is the core meaning of the present perfect.

questions.explanation:
El presente perfecto conecta una accion pasada con su consecuencia inmediata en el presente.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct negative form of the present perfect.

options.text: I not have seen that documentary.
options.feedback: The auxiliary must precede the adverb 'not'.

options.text: I have not saw that documentary.
options.feedback: After 'have not' the participle 'seen' is required.

options.text: I have not seen that documentary.
options.feedback: 'Have not seen' is the correct negative structure.

options.text: I did not saw that documentary.
options.feedback: That combines 'did' with an incorrect past form.

questions.explanation:
La negacion se forma con 'have/has not' seguido del participio. Es uno de los puntos mas frecuentes de las pruebas de esta unidad.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Look at the sentence: 'She has went to the coast last weekend.' What is the error?

options.text: Nothing is wrong with the sentence
options.feedback: Both the participle and the time expression are incorrect here.

options.text: 'Coast' must be capitalized
options.feedback: A common noun written with 'the' does not need a capital letter.

options.text: 'She' must be 'He'
options.feedback: The pronoun agrees with the rest of the sentence and poses no problem.

options.text: 'Went' is not a participle, and 'last weekend' requires the past simple
options.feedback: The correct form is 'She went to the coast last weekend'.

questions.explanation:
Hay dos errores: 'went' no es participo de 'go', y 'last weekend' es un tiempo pasado definido.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which verb forms its participle by changing 'e' to 'e'? Choose the correct irregular participle.

options.text: work - worked
options.feedback: "Work" is regular: it never changes before -ed, so its participle is simply "worked".

options.text: write - written
options.feedback: The irregular participle 'written' drops the base form's final structure.

options.text: open - opened
options.feedback: "Open" keeps its final -en unchanged and simply adds -d, giving "opened".

options.text: walk - walked
options.feedback: "Walk" already ends in -k and only takes -ed, so "walked" is not an irregular participle.

questions.explanation:
'Write' forma su participio como 'written', mientras los verbos regulares lo forman con -ed.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the text: 'When I arrived, the film ____ already ____.'
questions.context: Pasado simple y presente perfecto juntos, Cuenca.

options.text: has already start
options.feedback: The auxiliary would have to be 'had' with the participle 'started'.

options.text: already starts
options.feedback: The simple present would not place the action before the arrival.

options.text: had already started
options.feedback: The past perfect places the start before the arrival mentioned.

options.text: was already starting
options.feedback: The past continuous would not express completion before the arrival.

questions.explanation:
Un pasado simple y un presente perfecto pueden convivir: el segundo situa la accion antes del pasado simple.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Read: 'He has worked in three different countries, and he has never regretted the choice.' What can be inferred?
questions.context: Inferencia a partir del presente perfecto, Guayaquil.

options.text: He will change his job next year
options.feedback: No future event is mentioned in the text.

options.text: He values his decision up to this point
options.feedback: 'Has never regretted' covers the whole period up to now.

options.text: He was unhappy at the beginning
options.feedback: The text says he has never regretted it, which is the opposite.

options.text: He worked in those countries simultaneously
options.feedback: The text does not specify when each job took place.

questions.explanation:
La segunda parte indica que no hubo arrepentimiento hasta el momento actual, lo cual es una experiencia acumulada.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which question would you ask to find out about a person's experience?
questions.context: Tipos de pregunta sobre experiencia, Quito.

options.text: Have you ever worked abroad?
options.feedback: 'Have you ever' is the standard form for asking about experience.

options.text: Did you work abroad yesterday?
options.feedback: That question asks about a specific past time, not experience.

options.text: Do you work abroad?
options.feedback: That asks about a current or habitual situation.

options.text: Will you work abroad?
options.feedback: That asks about the future.

questions.explanation:
Las preguntas de experiencia se forman con 'have' mas participio y un marcador como 'ever' o 'never'.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the best sentence to describe the situation.
questions.context: Evaluacion de uso del presente perfecto, Cuenca.

options.text: I lived here since I was a child.
options.feedback: The simple past contradicts the ongoing meaning implied by 'since'.

options.text: I live here since I was a child.
options.feedback: The simple present is not compatible with 'since' plus a past reference.

options.text: I have lived here since I was a child.
options.feedback: 'Have lived since' marks a situation that started in the past and continues.

options.text: I was living here since I was a child.
options.feedback: The past continuous does not express a situation that continues.

questions.explanation:
El presente perfecto con 'since' describe una situacion que empezo en el pasado y sigue vigente.
